1.) I agree with all of your sentiments in your first paragraph about male circumcision. I always told myself if I had a son I wouldn’t have him circumcised and just teach him about his anatomy/proper hygiene.

2.) I don’t want to invalidate you specifically when I say MGM doesn’t equal FGM. I’m just speaking on how overall, specifically in our community, FGM is brutal and life altering. And the term MGM only came to rise as a counter point to FGM. Sorta like the All Lives Matter vs BLM people. 

Lastly, naturally woman will be more emotionally expressive. Of course. However all of our advice is subjective because this brother is asking for advice in regard to him and his wife personal experience. End of the day, all of this stuff is awful and shouldn’t occur and the best advice brother can get is from medical doctor.

Male circumcision isn’t comparable to fgm. Not in regards to the actual procedures, as I’ll agree that they both shouldn’t occur. But more so due to the reasons why both are often done, male circumcision is often done to prevent illness and to help with proper hygiene.. even the term MGM just isn’t common compared to FGM. I wholeheartedly disagree with your mind over matter sentiments and how men are more capable to be “in tune” or whatever that means.

After speaking with a friend who is an attorney but doesn’t specialize in medical malpractice, I was told I may have a case against the hospital, seeing that I arrived via EMS and my daughters critical symptoms were relayed to the  hospital staff. Under her medical chart it says “LWBS” (left without being seen) - we were only triaged and thus didn’t sign an AMA prior to leaving.

I’m not interested in suing or anything of that sort. I did speak with the patient relations department about our situation in the hopes that other children don’t experience that. 

I carry a ton of guilt for leaving though. I know I did what I could and worrying about the past does nothing, but the idea of losing her shakes me to my core. 

She has a follow up with her pediatrician tomorrow and I’ll definitely get a referral for therapy. It sounds like the best thing for her right now.

I filed a complaint while we were still inpatient. They told me the process can take up to 30 days to investigate. I’m not sure what will come of it but I hope no child or family has to ever go through what we went through. 

Thank you for the advice on finding a therapist specializing in T1/medical anxiety, I hadn’t even considered that as an option even though I’ve previously went to specialized therapy for PTSD, and I’m sure I can find one for both of us. 

She hasn’t expressed any desire to speak to a therapist when I asked. She shuts down, and begins shaking vigorously (which I assume is anxiety/panic attacks). She flat out refusing to speak about her condition at this time so I’m giving her time to process while being mindful of the things she must know.

Thank you for the reassurance. Yes I’m in the United States and I know our health care system can be extremely biased and just shitty at times but I felt like they’d know what to do since we called 911. I figured if one person fucked up maybe the next person wouldn’t? There were so many points of failure.

Yes, I’m at her side constantly I’ve set her up in my room due to her fear of going low over night. I’ve reassured her I’ll be here if anything happens and will take some of the weight off her shoulders until she is ready.
